seo_title: Cost of Living in Abu Dhabi 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Abu Dhabi per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of the UAE: visa-free entry for 90 days, zero income tax, high safety and modern infrastructure. Calmer and slightly cheaper than Dubai, though housing and everyday life are still expensive.
pros: Visa-free entry for 90 days, zero income tax
Calmer and greener than Dubai, yet with a capital-city standard of living
English is widely used, with strong healthcare and schools
Direct flights and a convenient aviation hub
cons: Expensive housing and everyday life, as everywhere in the UAE
Extreme summer heat (+45), life spent in air conditioning
Conservative norms of behaviour and dress code

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Abu Dhabi?
faq.answer: No, visa-free for up to 90 days per six months. To live and work you obtain a residence visa and an Emirates ID.

faq.question: Is it expensive to live in Abu Dhabi?
faq.answer: Yes: rent and everyday life are expensive, like in Dubai, but there is no income tax. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: How is Abu Dhabi different from Dubai?
faq.answer: Calmer, greener and slightly cheaper on rent, but less party-oriented and dynamic.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Abu Dhabi?
faq.answer: Russian cards don't work. People open a local account with an Emirates ID or pay with a foreign bank card.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Abu Dhabi?
faq.answer: Desert: very hot summers up to +45 with humidity, and a mild, comfortable winter.

faq.question: Is Abu Dhabi safe?
faq.answer: One of the safest cities in the world — low crime and strict laws.

reviews.text: I moved on a work visa: no taxes, safe, everything is new. Summer is brutal — the air conditioning saves you. Rent is paid in large sums upfront.
Abu Dhabi is calmer than Dubai, with the sea and culture. English is enough. It's expensive, but the quality of life is high.
